title: Why an 8 Meter Oarfish Can Drop Its Own Tail and Not Die
alt_titles: Doug Died 5 Times Near an Oarfish That Did Nothing
Why the Oarfish Can Cut Off Its Own Body and Not Die
The Creepiest Part of the Oarfish Lives Inside It
How Doug Died Getting Closer and Closer to an Oarfish
thumbnail_brief: A huge silver ribbon oarfish standing vertical in dark blue water, red crest at the top, filling the frame top to bottom, with tiny Doug at mid-height holding the cut-off end of its tail (clean rounded healed stump, no red) and looking at the camera, so the title's 'drop its own tail' gets its twist from IT LET GO (never OARFISH, DOOMSDAY, EARTHQUAKE, TAIL, DIE or any title word; blank-eyed, never smiling fish; no quake or disaster imagery; no size label over 8 m).
description:
The giant oarfish, the "doomsday fish" of Japanese earthquake legend, is the longest bony fish on Earth, and nearly every large one ever found is missing the back of its body: it cuts off its own tail end, more than once, and keeps swimming. Doug gets closer to an oarfish one step at a time, from a doomsday headline 9,000 km away to a sea-serpent sighting, a beach stranding, a fish that stands upright, a toothless mouth, silver skin, the missing half and finally the inside of its gut, where something else already lives.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe. Doug's death counter only goes up, and the oarfish's tail never grows back.

Florida Museum of Natural History, oarfish species profile: https://www.floridamuseum.ufl.edu/discover-fish/species-profiles/oarfish/
FishBase, Regalecus glesne (autotomy, the lost part is never regenerated): https://fishbase.se/summary/Regalecus-glesne
Kuris et al. (2015), Journal of Parasitology, parasites of the Catalina oarfish: https://complete.bioone.org/journals/journal-of-parasitology/volume-101/issue-1/14-581.1/Monsters-of-the-Sea-Serpent--Parasites-of-an-Oarfish/10.1645/14-581.1.full

— DISCLAIMER —
Educational entertainment. All animals and deaths are cartoon depictions; oarfish are not known to harm people, and a 2019 study found no reliable link between oarfish sightings and earthquakes.

— AI USE —
The narration is an AI text-to-speech voice. Scripts are researched and written with AI assistance and fact-checked against the sources above. All drawings are original.
